checklist: Eyes sit near the upper third.

checklist: Face and eyes are the main anchors.
The head is close without cutting hair or chin.
Background edges are clean.
The camera angle avoids strong distortion.

checklist: Faces stay readable and close enough.
The two-person mass is balanced around center.
Face height sits near the upper third.
Shoulders and hands are not awkwardly cropped.
teacherNotes: Keep a small group close enough that faces remain readable.
Balance both people around the center without making the frame static.
Keep shared face height near the upper third.

checklist: Horizon or dominant horizontal line is level.
Horizon sits on an upper or lower third.
Leading lines or foreground depth guide the eye.
Any person in the frame supports the scene scale.
teacherNotes: Place the horizon on an upper or lower third instead of the exact middle.
Use lines and perspective to lead the eye through the scene.
Keep strong horizontal elements level.

checklist: The focal object is obvious.
The subject sits near a third or intersection.
Props create balance without clutter.
Edges and background distractions are cropped out.
teacherNotes: Arrange objects so the focal point is obvious.
Place the focal point near rule-of-thirds lines or intersections.
Remove distracting background clutter around the subject.

checklist: The object clearly dominates the frame.
Viewpoint makes shape and scale understandable.
Negative space does not compete with the subject.
Background clutter is minimized.
teacherNotes: Frame the object as the clear subject of interest.
Try a viewpoint that makes an ordinary object more interesting.
Crop non-essential clutter from the frame.

checklist: The action or story is immediately readable.
Look or motion space is left in front of the subject.
The subject is close enough for the moment to read.
The background stays simple.
teacherNotes: Show people doing something rather than forcing a posed shot.
Move close enough that the action is understandable.
Keep the composition simple so the story reads quickly.

checklist: The frame is level and stable.
The subject is separated from harsh bright or dark patches.
The composition stays simple because detail is weaker.
Capture waits for a steady pose.
teacherNotes: Use a stable, simple composition when weak light makes detail harder to read.
Keep the subject separated from distracting bright or dark background areas.
Hold the frame level before capture.
